RESOLUTION ____-22 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS TO APPLY 
FOR THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE COMPREHENSIVE OPIOID, 
STIMULANT, AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE SITE-BASED PROGRAM GRANT 
 
 
WHEREAS The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) Office of Justice Programs is committed to 
advancing work that promotes civil rights and racial equity, increases access to justice, supports 
crime victims and individuals impacted by the justice system, strengthens community safety and 
protects the public from crime and evolving threats, and builds trust between law enforcement 
and the community; and  
 
WHEREAS, The Comprehensive Opioid, Stimulant, and Substance Abuse Program (COSSAP) 
supports states, units of local government, and tribal governments to plan, develop, and implement 
comprehensive efforts that identify, respond to, treat, and support those impacted by illicit opioids, 
stimulants, and other drugs.by illicit opioids, stimulants, and other drugs; and 
 
WHEREAS, COSSAP provides necessary resources that allow communities to respond to illicit 
substance use and misuse to reduce overdose deaths; promote public safety; and support access to 
prevention, harm-reduction, treatment, and recovery services in the community and justice system. 
The COSSAP also promotes cross-system planning and coordination to deliver a broad range of 
evidence-based, culturally relevant interventions; and 
 
WHEREAS, Navajo County Criminal Justice Coordinating Council was established in 2014 to 
expand and integrate services for persons with a mental illness and/or substance abused engaged in 
the criminal justice system. The Council consists of the County Attorney, County Sheriff, Jail 
Commander, Assistant County Manager, Public Defender, Judge, Court Administration, Probation, 
Behavioral Health Providers, and Regional Behavioral Health organizations; and 
  
WHEREAS, National Association of Drug Court Professionals (NADCP), a 501c3 non-profit 
organization, provides training services and proven strategies in judicial systems that empower 
people to change their lives; and 
 
WHEREAS, Community Bridges, Inc. (CBI), an integrated behavioral healthcare agency, uses a 
holistic/integrated approach to addiction treatment and behavioral health concerns and collaborates 
with Navajo County to serve our community; and 
 
WHEREAS, in partnership with NADCP and CBI, the County’s Criminal Justice Coordinating

County Overdose Prevention and Engagement (COPE) program with the grant, and enhance the 
County’s criminal justice system with the proposed project. In order to apply for DOJ grants, 
Navajo County needs to create an account with JustGrants, the DOJ’s grants management system.  
 
NOW, THEREFORE , BE IT RESOLVED BY TH E NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF 
SUPERVISORS AS FOLLOWS:  
 
• That Navajo County requests $1.3 million from the COSSAP grant program  for 
development of a County Overdose Prevention and Engagement (COPE) program and 
identifies NADCP and CBI as subgrant recipients in the project proposal.  
• That Jayson Vowell, Finance Director, is the assigned Entity Administrator role on behalf 
of Navajo County, who conforms information contained in the Entity Profile is current, and 
manages entity users, including user role assignments in DIAMD, and specific application 
and award-level assignments in JustGrants.

who submits programmatic-related award requirements, including Performance Reports, 
certain GAMs, and portions of the Closeout. 
• That Ken Maruyama, Strategic Initiatives Manager, have the assigned  Alternate Grant

• That Dawnafe Whitesinger , Chairwoman & Supervisor, is the assigned Authorized

• That Jayson Vowell is the assigned  Financial Manager role, who certifies and submits

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. a.        
Meeting Date: 06/14/2022  
Title: RFP No.B22-01-024 Work Management & Asset Inventory System
Submitted For: John Osgood, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Jeanine Carruthers, Deputy Director Administration
Department: Public Works
Presented By: John Osgood
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of award of Contract No. B22-01-024 Work Order Management & Asset Inventory
System to MaintStar, Inc.
Background:
The purpose of this contract is to provide a Work Order Management and Asset Inventory
Tracking System (WMATS) for its Building Permits, Engineering/Flood Control, Sign
Management, Highway Management, Fuel Management, Motor Pool Vehicle Reservations,
Planning & Zoning, and E911/Rural Addressing.  Sealed proposals were received by the Board of
Supervisors at the Navajo County Governmental Center, Holbrook, Arizona until 3:00 PM,
M.S.T., March 16, 2022, in strict accordance with the specifications on file in the office of the
Navajo County Department of Public Works. No proposals were accepted after 3:00 PM, M.S.T. 
The proposals were publicly opened at 3:15 PM.  Four proposals were received.  The Evaluation
Committee evaluated the proposals and short listed two highest ranking proposals. 
Interviews/System Demonstrations were conducted on May 17, 2022 with the two shortlisted
vendors.  The Evaluation Committee evaluated the Interviews/System Demonstrations and is
recommending award of contract to MaintStar, Inc. as the highest ranking vendor.
MaintStar has a 37-year track record and their products are used by over 200 government agencies
in the United States and Canada. MaintStar offers their Enterprise Asset Management System
(EAMS) product for Public Works and the Land Management System (LMS) for Permitting,
Planning, etc.  The EAMS and LMS have a seamless integration of Public Works and Land
Management Operations.
A few of MaintStar EAMS key features: 
It has full asset inventory capabilities and is linked to the Work Order and Work
Management functions and GIS.
Supports the use of assets for CIP budgeting and planning, rehabilitation and replacement
of  and Preventative Maintenance.
Support updates of asset inventory condition, installation dates, based on data and ratings
from Work Orders and Inspection records.
Alerts/Notifications can be set up in both desktop and mobile applications.
Mobile Integration for Utilization by Field Crews.

<!-- page 616 -->
Mobile Integration for Utilization by Field Crews.
Citizens can report concerns by either using the Citizen Public Portal or MaintStar Mobile
Citizen.
A few of MaintStar's LMS key features: 
GIS-centric approach to Land Management with a visual and efficient approach to
processing community development activities.
On-Board electronic plan review.
Mobile Inspections.
On-Board Workflow Automation manages all aspects of the application, review, issuance,
and enforcement life-cycle.
Electronic notifications, alerts and task reminders.
Community Engagement Portal offers a configurable web portal for applications, status,
document uploads and fees payment.
Recommendation: 
The Evaluation Committee is recommending award of Contract No. B22-01-024 Work Order
Management & Asset Inventory System to MaintStar, Inc.

stepping down from his role as of June 14, 2022 and is recognized for his years of service to
Navajo County.

Title: Old West RV and Boat Storage Facility, District IV.
Submitted For: John Osgood, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Berrin Nejad, Community Development Director
Department: Public Works Division: Planning & Zoning
Presented By: Berrin Nejad
Motion before the Board:
PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration and adoption of Resolution Number 18-2022
approving/denying a Special Use Permit request for Old West RV and Boat Storage with 113
spaces. 
Background:
APN #206-15-025, T12N, R17E, S29.  Owner: Mark Dahl.
The applicant is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit for an RV and Boat Storage facility. 
The access is off Highway 260 and will have a 70-foot setback for customers to turn in without
impacting the highway traffic. The applicant also owns the 6 acres to the south of the site.
 
The facility will be an open-air storage with 113 spaces and will be open to store travel trailers,
Class A motor homes, toy haulers or fishing boats. The facility will also have an RV dump
station, potable water, and a commercial trash receptacle.
 
The size of each space is 12x20, 12x35, and 12x45. The drive aisles are 30’ wide with pull-thru
for each space at a 60-degree angle, which makes maneuverability easy on the site.
 
The drainage is naturally to the Northeast and there will be a drainage basin placed along the
property line on the east fence to accommodate any runoff from the property which will flow to
ADOT’s drainage infrastructure along State Route 260.
 
The hours of the operation will be 7 am to 5 pm, Monday through Saturday.  The facility will be
closed on Sundays.  The gate will be open during business hours and closed after hours with
keypad entry.   The lighting for after hours will be placed for the customers and safety, that will
be LED and shielding will be contained on the property.
There will be a 4 x 8’sign with 5-inch lettering near the entrance, at the gate, reflecting the rustic
Old West theme.
 
A metal-tree rail fence will be around the property.  On the west side, a corrugated steel privacy
fence will be placed.  On the north and east sides, a green belt will be placed containing trees.

<!-- page 628 -->
fence will be placed.  On the north and east sides, a green belt will be placed containing trees. 
 
There will be trees planted in the front and on the north side, also utilizing the drainage water,
while buffering from the adjacent property and the highway.
 
Phase II will have an RV Parts store.  Currently, the closest part-stores are either in Show Low or
in Payson. The applicant plans to develop the project and be operational in the summer of 2022.
 
The staff received one (1) support letter for the proposal.
The Planning and Zoning Commission heard this item in their May 19, 2022, public meeting and
after hearing presentations and comments, made a motion to recommend approval of the Special
Use Permit to the BOS with a 6-0 vote. 
Recommendation: 
The Planning and Zoning Commission and staff recommend approval of this project and a Special
Use Permit request.

NAVAJO COUNTY 
 
               COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT 
       
PLANNING and ZONING COMMISSION 
 
 
STAFF REPORT  
 
 
 
TO: Planning and Zoning Commission 
 
FROM: Berrin Nejad, Community Development Director 
  
HEARING DATE: May 19, 2022   
 
PROJECT NUMBER:   SUP 22-004  OLD WEST RV and BOAT STORAGE, DISTRICT 
IV: A request for a Special Use Permit to construct an RV and boat 
storage facility with 113 spaces. The property is 4.58 acres in size, 
located east of Highway 260 in Overgaard. APN# 206-15-025, T12N, 
R17E, S29.  Owner: Mark Dahl. 
 
 
BACKGROUND and ANALYSIS: 
The applicant is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit for a n RV and Boat Storage facility.  
The access is off Highway 260 and will have a 70-foot setback for the customers to turn in without 
impacting the highway traffic. The applicant also owns the 6 acres to the South of the site. 
 
The facility will be an open-air storage with 113 spaces and will be open to store travel trailers, Class 
A motorhomes, toy haulers or fishing boats. The facility will also have an RV dump station, potable 
water, and a commercial trash receptacle.  
 
The size of each space is 12x20, 12x35, and 12x45. The drive aisles are 30’ wide with pull thru for 
each space at a 60-degree angle that makes maneuverability easy on the site.  
 
The drainage is naturally to the Northeast and there will be a drainage basin placed along the property 
line on the east fence to accommodate any runoff from the property which will also flow towards to 
ADOT’s drainage along State Route 260. 
 
The hours of the operation wi ll be 7 am to 5 pm, Monday through Saturday .  The facility  will be 
closed on Sundays.  The gate will be open during the business hours and closed after hours with 
keypad entry.   The lighting for afterhours will be placed for the customers and safety that will be 
LED and shielding will be contained in the property.

<!-- page 641 -->
Planning and Zoning Commission                                     May 19, 2022        2 | P a g e  
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
LAND USE: 
 
Description and Character of Surrounding Area 
The site is on the east side of Highway 260 in Overgaard and the property is surrounded by the 
same type of zoning  which is  C-R Commercial -Residential first 300 feet from H wy 260 and 
remaining portion being R1-10 residential. The two lots on the north side of the property are 
currently vacant, the property on South is an open area with the applicant’s residence in the back 
half of the property, owned by the applicant.  
 
 
Adjacent Land Uses and Zoning 
North:   C-R and R1-10 Vacant 
South:   C-R and R1-10 – Residential house in the back portion of the property 
East:    Highway 260 and Post Office and other commercial uses across highway 
 
West:  A-General – Residential house 
 
There will be a 4 x 8’sign with 5 -inch lettering near the entrance, at the gate, reflecting the rustic 
Old West theme.  
 
A metal three rail fence will be around the property.  On the west side, a corrugated steel privacy 
fence will be placed.  On the North and East side, green belt will be placed containing trees.   
 
There will be trees planted in the front and on the north side, also utilizing the drainage water, while 
buffering from the adjacent property and the highway.  
 
Phase II will have an RV Parts store.  Currently, the closest part stores are in either in Show Low or 
in Payson. The applicant plans to develop the project and be operational in the summer of 2022.  
 
The staff received one (1) support letter on the proposal.

APPLICABLE CODES: 
 
Zoning Ordinance: Navajo County, Zoning Ordinance addresses Manufactured Home Parks in the 
following areas:  
 
ARTICLE 15 – (C-R) COMMERCIAL-RESIDENTIAL ZONING DISTRICT 
Section 1501 – Purpose  
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to provide for shops and services in convenient 
locations to meet the daily needs of families in the immediate residential neighborhoods and 
wholesaling or distribution activities in locations where there is adequate access to major streets or 
highways.  Principal uses permitted in this zoning district include retail and wholesale commerce, 
commercial entertainment, and some uses of a light manufacturing nature.

Section 2001 – Special Uses 
32. Storage of manufactured homes, travel trailers, boats and aircraft.

34. Warehousing and storage, mini storage , including outdoor storage, i.e., recreational and 
equipment storage, public utilities, but not including the warehousing and storage of explosives or 
junk. 
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
 
1. The item has been properly noticed and posted in compliance with Arizona Revised 
Statutes and Article 29.  
Notice of this item was published in the May 4, 2022 The Tribune.   Physical postings were made 
on the property on May 4, 2022 and postcards were mailed to all neighbors within 300 feet. 
 
2. The proposal is in compliance with the Comprehensive Plan. 
 This proposal meets policies and goals as laid out by Navajo County’s Comprehensive Plan. 
 
3. The proposed use is compatible with the permissible uses in the zoning district in which 
the property is located. 
This property is zoned C-R Commercial- Residential and similar type of commercial uses are in 
the area.  An RV and boat storage facility is compatible with permissible uses in this zoning 
district and surrounding uses.  
 
4. The proposed use is compatible with the current and likely future uses of properties in the 
vicinity of the proposed use. 
An RV and boat storage facility would be compatible in the area.   
 
5. The proposed use will have minimal adverse effects on the public health, safety, and general 
welfare of properties in the vicinity of the proposed use. 
With the proper screening, meeting the vis ion triangle rules, there should be little to no issues 
for health, safety, or welfare for nearby properties.

Deputy County Attorney has reviewed the proposed Site Plan  and supports Staff’s 
recommendations.                         Initial: B.S.C.   
           
 
PLANNING AND ZONING:

Planning and Zoning Staff recommends that the Planning and Zoning Commission recommend 
approval of Special Use Permit on APN# 206-15-025 to the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, 
subject to the following conditions:  
1. The applicant shall obtain any required Navajo County permits, including, but not limited to, 
building, sewer connection, grading, drainage, and sign permits. 
2. All the corners shall be according to vision triangle rules and regulations. No building or 
fencing shall obstruct the view of the traffic.  
3. No building or structure shall not be occupied prior to complete compliance with all 
appropriate Building Department requirements. 
4. All lighting on the property shall shielded to reflect downward, be motion-activated, and be 
in conformance with the Navajo County Lighting Ordinance. 
5. Hours of operation shall be 7 am to 5 pm Monday through Saturday and closed on Sundays.  
The gate will be closed, but the site shall be accessible with a keypad entry.  
6. The traffic flow shall not be affected by the vehicles that are trying to access to the facility 
at any time. A recessed gate location shall allow the pull ins and turn arounds.  
7. The permitted Special Use shall be allowed to occur per the attached/approved site plan.  Any 
expansion or change of the Special Use shall require an amendment to this Permit. 
8. This Special Use Permit shall run with the land pending compliance with all County, State, 
and Federal requirements.

Certificate of Occupancy:

April 12, 2022 
 
 
To whom it may concern.  
 
My family and I are full time residents of Overgaard Arizona. 
 
We have come to love and appreciate Overgaard with all of its many different facets including the many 
retired citizens and the second home residents. The one constant in this community is the desire to be 
here for the beauty and cooler temperatures. This brings in a great amount of family and friends to the 
area. 
 
A large part of the transient population stays in their Recreational Vehicles. In an effort to mitigate 
expense, time and travel many leave their R.V.s in their family or friends’ driveways or elsewhere on 
their property for the season. 
 
This dynamic as I have been told, although convenient, is not ideal for the homeowner. Or neighbors. 
 
Facilities, that could store these vehicles in between times is a much-needed business, that will bring 
monies to local area. I feel it is a responsible step in our community’s development to provide for this 
need. 
 
I support this project and it's plan as an asset to our community. 
 
Tim Phelps

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. c. 1. a.        
Meeting Date: 06/14/2022  
Title: IGA City of Winslow for the USACE Winslow Levee Project
Submitted For: John Osgood, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: John Osgood, Public Works Director
Department: Public Works
Presented By: John Osgood
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of the Intergovernmental Agreement with the City of Winslow for Planning,
Design and Cost Sharing the Little Colorado River Flood Risk Management Project. 
Background:
As discussed over the years with the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, the Winslow Levee has
been decertified since 2008; its  failing condition is a flood risk to surrounding communities and
the BNSF rail line that moves billions of dollars of goods through Arizona each year. The
completion of the ten-year-long United States Army Corps of Engineers Feasiblility Study and
accompanying Chief of Engineers report transmitted to the Secretary of the Army in December,
2018 was a significant milestone in the effort to rehabilitate the levee.  In January of this year,
Navajo County and the City of Winslow learned of the most recent and most important milestone
in the life of the project to date - that the national bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs
law (IIJL) act, which provides $8.3 billion for building and strengthening aging water
infrastructure and dam safety throughout the American West, allocated $65.75M to the USACE
for full funding of design and construction of the Little Colorado River Flood Control Project at 
Winslow, AZ.  The IGA for your consideration establishes the roles and responsibilities of the
Navajo County Flood Control District as the non-federal sponsor for the USACE project and the
City of Winslow as a key stakeholder and partner in the project; administration of construction and
identification of funding for such construction shall be confirmed by a separate written agreement.
Staff will present the IGA and answer any questions at the June 14th meeting of the Board of
Supervisors.
 
 
 
Recommendation: 
Approve the Intergovernmental Agreement with the City of Winslow.

<!-- page 670 -->
Approve the Intergovernmental Agreement with the City of Winslow.

INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENT  
between  
NAVAJO COUNTY  FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT  
and 
THE CITY OF WINSLOW   
for PLANNING , DESIGN & COST SHARING  
the LITTLE COLORADO RIVER FLOOD RISK MANAGEMENT PROJECT    
THIS INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENT (“IGA”) is entered into as of JUNE 14, 2022 (the “Effective 
Date”) by and between NAVAJO COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT, a political subdivision of the State 
of Arizona acting by and through its Board of Directors (the “NCFCD”) and the CITY OF WINSLOW, an 
Arizona municipal corporation acting by and through its Mayor and City Council (the “City”).  
1. PURPOSE 
The Purpose of this IGA is to formalize roles and responsibilities of Navajo County and the City of 
Winslow related to the Little Colorado River at Winslow, Navajo County, Arizona, Flood Risk 
Management Project (the “project”).  This Agreement embodies the parties’ unequivocal 
commitment to partnering on the project on behalf of current and future Navajo County and 
City of Winslow residents and businesses residing in and near the floodplain, and the parties’ 
entire understanding with respect to its subject matter, superseding all prior understandings, 
whether oral or written, with respect to the same subject matter.  
 
2. EFFECTIVE DATE AND TERM 
This Agreement shall remain in effect from the date of the signing of the agreement until 
terminated by the parties in writing in accordance with Section 7 below.  This agreement is also 
terminable in accordance with the provisions of A.R.S. § 38-511, and that statute is hereby 
incorporated into this agreement by reference.   
3. TERMS, CONDITIONS, AND FINANCING 
a. The NCFCD, as the non-federal local sponsor of the project, shall be the lead agency in all 
matters related to the project.  The NCFCD and the City will collaborate on all 
communication with the United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE); Arizona’s federal 
Congressional leadership; state, federal and tribal governments and agencies; and other key 
stakeholders.  Once the NCFCD and City have collaborated as stated above, all official 
communications related to the project will be transmitted solely by the NCFCD to these 
entities and others as necessary to facilitate project development. 
b. The City, as the project’s most involved stakeholder, will support the project in financial, 
legal and logistical matters to reduce: risk of property damages; incidents impacting life-

<!-- page 672 -->
safety; health risks; and negative economic impacts associated with and caused by flooding 
from the Little Colorado River. 
c. The NCFCD and City may engage consultants to provide expertise on matters relevant to 
moving the project to and through construction.  To the greatest extent possible, all project-
specific meetings and communications with any elected official, staff or representative of an 
agency mentioned in paragraph a. of this section shall be communicated between NCFCD 
and the City prior to scheduling meetings and generating communications.     
d. The project shall consist of multiple phases.  The cost sharing formula for each phase of the 
project is as follows:  sixty-five percent (65%) federal share and thirty-five percent (35%) 
non-federal share. As the project moves forward, the NCFCD and the City agree to share 
equally in the non-federal project costs associated with executing required agreements; the 
pre-construction, planning and design (PED) phase; and construction costs incurred by the 
Navajo County Flood Control District in its role as the sole non-federal sponsor.   
e. The NCFCD will develop a transparent financial tracking and reporting process for managing 
project funding and expenditures as recognized by the Government Finance Officers 
Association of the United States & Canada.  Non-federal sponsor project billings from and 
payments to USACE will be handled by NCFCD.   
f. The NCFCD and the City will communicate and share key information about the project as it 
progresses. 
g. This IGA is not intended to create any right, benefit, or trust, substantive or procedural, 
enforceable at law or equity, by any party or non-party to this IGA against Navajo County 
Flood Control District or the City, or their respective agencies, officers, Councilmembers or 
any other person. 
h. This Agreement may be amended (including any modification of the scope, funding or 
responsibilities of the parties) only in a document which expressly refers to it and is 
executed and approved with the same formality by both parties. 
i. None of the activities or information generated pursuant to this IGA shall require either 
party to obligate or encumber funds or assets; however not doing so may impact the ability 
to construct the project.  
 
4. SEVERABILITY 
If any portion of this Agreement is found to be unenforceable by a court of competent 
jurisdiction, the remaining terms and provisions unaffected thereby shall remain in full force and 
effect. 
 
5. ALTERNATIVE DISPUTE RESOLUTION 
a. In the event of a disagreement between the parties regarding the interpretation of this 
Agreement or their respective obligations under this Agreement, the parties agree that they 
will first make efforts to resolve the matter through alternative dispute resolution prior to 
proceeding to litigation in Court.

<!-- page 673 -->
b. In the event of a dispute that the parties are unable to resolve through the use of an 
alternative dispute resolution process, it is agreed that the Courts of Navajo County, 
Arizona, shall have exclusive jurisdiction and be the appropriate venue for resolving the 
matter. 
 
6. INDEMNIFICATION  
Each party shall be responsible for its own liability arising from the acts or omissions of its 
employees, or agents occurring in the course of performing this Agreement. Neither party 
agrees to assume any liability of the other, or to defend, indemnify, or hold harmless the other 
party, against any claims of the other party, or liability of the other party, arising from the other 
party’s performance of the Agreement. Instead, all rights to indemnify and contribution 
between the parties to this Agreement shall be as provided by the law of the State of Arizona. 
7. TERMINATION 
Termination of this IGA will not affect the parties’ rights and authorities necessary to perform 
the actions, functions, and/or services attendant to the execution, administration, and 
expiration or termination of this IGA.   
a. Cancellation at Will 
Either party may terminate this IGA upon written notice to the other party at least ninety 
(90) days before the effective date of termination. Notice to the County shall be addressed 
to the Navajo County Manager and notice to the City shall be addressed to the Winslow City 
Manager.   
 
b. Agreed Cancellation 
This IGA may be canceled by mutual agreement.  
 
c. Violation of Agreement 
Either party may terminate this IGA if a violation of any of the terms and conditions by the 
other party remains uncured thirty (30) days after the terminating party has delivered to the 
violating party a written notice specifying the nature of the violation. 
 
8. APPROPRIATION 
The parties agree their respective share of funding for PED is budgeted and available for use as 
required by USACE.  The parties agree to work through their respective public budget and 
administrative processes to identify funding sources for future phases of the project including 
construction.    This IGA sets forth the parties’ responsibilities for planning, design and cost sharing 
for the project. Not hing in this IGA shall govern responsibilities for project construction.  
Administration of construction and identification of funding for such construction shall be 
confirmed by separate written agreement.

<!-- page 674 -->
9. AUTHORIZATION 
Each party warrants and represents that each official who executes this Agreement on its behalf 
is fully and duly authorized to do so and that when so executed this Agreement will be a valid 
and binding obligation of the party.  Technical and Administrative contacts: 
Navajo County Flood Control District contact: 
   Glenn Kephart, Navajo County Manager 
 
   City of Winslow contact: 
John Barkley, City of Winslow City Manager

pursuant to resolutions duly adopted by their respective governing boards.

Motion before the Board:
EXECUTIVE SESSION pursuant to A.R.S. §38-431.03(A)(3) for the Board to receive legal
advice from its attorney regarding a briefing on Arizona Republican Party v. Hobbs, Mohave
County Case No. CV-202200594. 
Background:
The Arizona Republican Party has filed suit in Mohave County against the Arizona Secretary of
State and elections officials from all fifteen Arizona counties seeking to end all forms of early
voting in the State of Arizona for the 2022 election and beyond.  Although the Board of
Supervisors is not named as a party to the action, a board briefing is necessary to discuss the
potential impacts of the lawsuit and the Navajo County Recorder's defense of the case.
Recommendation: 
No action by the Board is requested at this time.
